note.p: Godwin sent (from him and his friend) £10 in 1798 to help a woman in distress to move to Jedburgh through Agnes Hall - who then related that the woman's two elder children had died from the croup and that the money had been used to relieve their suffering. The distressed woman's husband was in a regiment in the West Indies.

There is no evidence of any of this activity in Godwin's diary entries around this time. The only references to Agnes Hall are on 26 February 1827 and 14 February 1834. We cannot be sure that they are identical.

Ed Pope notes: Agnes C Hall DNB 1775/6-1846 was probably the A C Hall of 1807 and the Agnes Hall of 1827 and 1834, also perhaps the two calls on mrs Hall in 1808. Her letter to Godwin dated 9.5.1799 from Jedburgh is in Bodleian Abinger c4 f111-2 and Godwins letter to her of 23.2.1798 is in Bodleian Abinger c22 f94-5 or c54 f72. She may have also been some of the later mrs Hall entries and her husband Robert Hall DNB 1763-1824 may possibly have appeared in the diary as a plain Hall entry.
See ODNB: Hall [née Scott], Agnes C. [pseud. Rosalia St Clair] (1775/6–1846), writer and translator.
